title: Exact PCG state, output and advance for all four generator types
explanation: For rand_pcg 0.10.2, the four state getters return their stored word. The three LCG stream getters return increment>>1; from_state preserves its input state and stores increment=(stream<<1) OR 1, discarding the highest stream bit. Their new constructors initialize state=((input_state+increment)*multiplier+increment) with modular arithmetic; the multipliers are 6364136223846793005, 47026247687942121848144207491837523525 and 15750249268501108917 respectively. Mcg128Xsl64::new stores input_state OR 1. Native output proofs retain Lcg64Xsh32::try_next_u32 and both word widths for the three 128-bit types. The XSL-RR variants permute the newly advanced state; CM-DXSM permutes the old state then advances. Their 32-bit methods return the low 32 bits of the 64-bit result with the same final state. Original Result::map and conversion closures are body-extracted. Mcg128Xsl64::advance additionally terminates normally for every u128 delta and every internal u128 state, returning state=M^delta*initial_state modulo 2^128, M=47026247687942121848144207491837523525. A well-founded halving-loop proof connects the original body to this ordinary power specification, covering all deltas without an artificial execution bound. These twenty-five direct original-body API guarantees apply under default and serde because the selected official translations are byte-identical; the serde implementations themselves remain unproved. Each of the three LCG advance methods also terminates normally for every full-width delta, state and increment, preserving the stored increment and producing exactly delta repetitions of the ordinary modular affine step x↦M*x+increment. An independent linear recurrence specifies this behavior; a generic affine-composition proof connects the original binary algorithm to it. Increments need not be odd for this state-transform identity. Separate Kani evidence calls the unchanged Mcg128Xsl64::from_seed and public state getter for every sixteen-byte seed. Its state equals the independently decoded little-endian u128 seed OR 1 (242 successful checks under each of default and serde). The exact rand_core 0.10.0 and serde 1.0.228 dependency lock is retained. This is a separate Kani body guarantee, not another Aeneas machine claim or a formal cross-tool equivalence proof. Separately, four Kani harnesses call the original manual Debug implementations through all typed inputs of the listed new/from_state/from_seed/seed_from_u64 constructors. Under default formatting and a fixed 64-byte writer that accepts all bytes or rejects the first write, they emit the fixed redacted type-name literal and propagate the writer error. All four baseline rand_core0.10.0 jobs complete with 8925 checks and no failures.
